newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - July 16.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- H&C DIRECTOR TO TAKE 1.3 MILLION STG

H&C Furnishings, which owns the Harveys home furnishings shops, has revealed that retiring deputy chief executive Nicholas Jeffrey will receive a total of 1.3m stg in compensation payments. The company has denied any dispute with Jeffrey, who will become a non-executive director of H&C Furnishings.
-- VILLA GETS IN BIND OVER TELEVISION CONTRACT TERMS

Doug Ellis, chairman of soccer club Aston Villa, has been forced to retract a statement made on Tuesday claiming the Premier League's new 670 million stg four-year television contract with BSkyB contains a break clause. Ellis told a press conference, called to announce Villa's financial results, that the clause would allow the league to break the contract after two years and renegotiate the terms. The retraction followed a complaint from BSkyB.
-- CAIRN AND SHELL SIGN ALLIANCE

Cairn, the UK independent oil and gas explorer, has signed definitive agreements with Shell over an alliance between the two companies in Bangladesh and parts of India. Under the deal, Shell has paid $65 million to acquire Holland Sea Search Bangladesh, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cairn, and taken an 18.75 percent stake in the Sangu gasfield.
THE TIMES
-- DRINKS GROUPS CONSIDER SPLITTING LVMH IN TWO

Senior executives from Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, the drinks giants who are planning a 23 billion stg merger, have held three-way talks in London with counterparts from LVMH, the French luxury goods firm, which is opposing the merger. It is reported that the two UK firms are considering a proposal from LVMH that would give them control over the French group's Hennessy cognac business.
-- GOLDEN SHARE IN BT ABANDONED

The government has withdrawn its golden share in British Telecom, ending an agreement made at the time of the company's privatisation that the state would hold the stake to protect the company from takeover. The move was prompted by a request from BT made just after the May 1 general election.
-- TIM SAINSBURY SELLS SHARES FOR 4.53 MILLION STG

Sir Tim Sainsbury, the former Conservative MP who is a non-executive director of supermarket chain J Sainsbury, has made 4.53 million stg by selling 1.05 million shares in the group. No reason has been given for the sale, which was completed last Friday. Sir Tim still owns almost 4 percent of the company.
THE GUARDIAN
-- CARRIER RESISTS EU CALL TO GIVE UP HEATHROW SLOTS FOR US
LINK

The annual meeting of British Airways has been told the airline is resisting demands from European Union regulators that it give up hundreds of landing slots at Heathrow as a condition to gain approval for the planned alliance with American Airlines. BA said it hoped the alliance would be cleared in time for the two airlines to begin working together by next summer.
-- BRUSSELS BACKS REBUFF OF BOEING PROPOSALS

The European Commission has issued a statement backing the tough stance taken by Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert over the proposed aerospace merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas. According to EU sources, Boeing representatives are returning to the US after failing to reach a compromise in talks with the EU over the $14 billion deal.
-- ACE CATALOGUE OF 1,000 ROCK'N'ROLL CLASSICS SOLD TO GRADE'S VCI

VCI, the independent book, CD and video firm, has paid 2 million stg to acquire the catalogue of Ace Records. The purchase gives VCI, chaired by former Channel 4 boss Michael Grade, record masters and publishing rights to about 1,000 rock-and-roll and r&b classics from the 1950s and 1960s.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SBC TO TAKE 340 MILLION STG STAKE IN JAPANESE BANK

Swiss Bank Corporation is to gain a pre-Big Bang foothold in Japan's financial services market by taking a 340 million stg stake in Long Term Credit Bank, the country's eighth largest bank. The investment will help LTCB recapitalise itself and will pair it with a heavyweight international banking partner.
-- PIFCO BID EXPECTED AS TALKS WITH KENWOOD BREAK DOWN

Electrical appliances group Pifco may launch a hostile takeover bid for rival manufacturer Kenwood after the breakdown on Tuesday of merger talks between the two groups. Pifco has been courting Kenwood for two years, and is understood to have had an offer that was pitched substantially above Kenwood's 118p current share price rejected.
-- ANITE REVEALS 600,000 STG PAY-OFF AS ITS PRE-TAX LOSSES
TRIPLE

Anite, the data communications and software group, has reported a near-tripling of pre-tax losses for the year to end-April, to 50.4 million stg. The losses included a 32.2 million stg hit on surplus properties. The company also revealed that Jon Richards, who resigned as chief executive in March, could receive compensation totalling up to 600,000 stg.
